name: Pasta with tomato sauce
summary: Penne tossed with homemade tomato sauce, finished with Parmesan and basil.
method: Cook the 180 g dry penne in a large pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, or as the pack says, until al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Meanwhile warm the tomato sauce in a small saucepan.
Toss the penne with the sauce, adding a splash of the cooking water to loosen. Serve with the Parmesan grated over and torn basil if you like.
notes: Times assume the tomato pasta sauce is already made.

name: Pasta arrabbiata
summary: Penne in tomato sauce spiked with garlic and chilli fried in olive oil.
method: Cook the 180 g dry penne in a large pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, or as the pack says, until al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Meanwhile warm the olive oil in a frying pan over a low heat, add the thinly sliced garlic and the chilli flakes and let them sizzle gently for 1 to 2 minutes without browning.
Add the tomato sauce and simmer for 3 minutes, then toss in the penne with a splash of the cooking water. Scatter with the chopped parsley.
notes: A variant of pasta with tomato sauce: garlic and chilli fried in oil replace the Parmesan and basil.

name: Pasta with tuna and tomato
summary: Fusilli in tomato sauce with flaked tinned tuna, capers and parsley.
method: Cook the 180 g dry fusilli in a large pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, or as the pack says, until al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Meanwhile warm the tomato sauce in a small saucepan, stir in the capers and the drained tuna (one tin) in large flakes and heat through for 3 minutes.
Toss with the fusilli and a splash of the cooking water. Finish with the chopped parsley and the lemon zest if using.
notes: A variant of pasta with tomato sauce with tinned tuna and capers added. Uses tuna in oil, drained; tuna in water, drained, has less fat.

name: Chicken and tomato pasta
summary: Pan-fried chicken breast and spinach in tomato sauce with penne and Parmesan.
method: Cook the 180 g dry penne in a large pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, or as the pack says, until al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.

Meanwhile cut the chicken breast into bite-sized pieces and season with the salt and black pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan and fry the chicken over a medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Pour in the tomato sauce and simmer for 3 minutes, then stir in the spinach until wilted.
Toss with the penne and a splash of the cooking water, and serve with the Parmesan grated over.
notes: A variant of pasta with tomato sauce with chicken and spinach added.

name: Gnocchi with tomato sauce
summary: Homemade potato gnocchi tossed in tomato sauce with Parmesan and basil.
method: Warm the tomato sauce in a wide pan.
Cook the gnocchi in a large pan of boiling water until they float, then 1 minute more. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
Toss the gnocchi gently in the sauce and serve with the Parmesan grated over and torn basil.
notes: A variant of pasta with tomato sauce, with potato gnocchi in place of pasta. Times assume the gnocchi and sauce are made.

name: Pasta puttanesca
summary: Spaghetti in a punchy tomato sauce with anchovies, black olives, capers and chilli.
method: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a low heat. Add the sliced garlic, the anchovies and the chilli flakes and stir for 2 minutes until the anchovies melt.
Add the chopped tomatoes and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes until thickened, then stir in the halved black olives and the capers.
Cook the 180 g dry spaghetti in a large pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, or as the pack says, until al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Toss the spaghetti in the sauce with a splash of the cooking water and scatter with the chopped parsley.

name: Pasta with pesto
summary: Fusilli coated in homemade basil pesto, loosened with the pasta water.
method: Cook the 180 g dry fusilli in a large pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, or as the pack says, until al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Return the fusilli to the warm pan off the heat, add the pesto and 2 to 3 tablespoons of the cooking water and toss until glossy; do not heat the pesto or it will darken.
Serve with extra Parmesan grated over if you like.
notes: Uses three servings (about 85 g) of the basil pesto component. With a jar of pesto, log the jar weight instead.

name: Pasta with garlic and olive oil
summary: Spaghetti tossed with gently fried garlic, chilli flakes, parsley and olive oil.
method: Cook the 180 g dry spaghetti in a large pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, or as the pack says, until al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Meanwhile warm the olive oil in a large frying pan over a low heat, add the thinly sliced garlic and the chilli flakes and cook gently for 2 to 3 minutes until the garlic is pale gold, not brown.
Add the spaghetti, a good splash of the cooking water, the chopped parsley and the salt, and toss over the heat for 1 minute until the oil and water turn into a light sauce that clings.

name: Pasta with butter and Parmesan
summary: Egg tagliatelle glossed with butter, pasta water and plenty of Parmesan.
method: Cook the 160 g dry egg tagliatelle in a large pan of boiling water for 6 to 8 minutes, or as the pack says. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Melt the butter in the empty pan over a low heat with 4 tablespoons of the cooking water, swirling to make a creamy emulsion.
Add the tagliatelle and the finely grated Parmesan and toss quickly until every strand is coated, adding more cooking water if it looks dry. Finish with black pepper.

name: Spaghetti bolognese
summary: Spaghetti with homemade beef bolognese sauce and Parmesan.
method: Reheat the bolognese sauce in a small saucepan until bubbling hot.
Cook the 180 g dry spaghetti in a large pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, or as the pack says, until al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Toss the spaghetti with the sauce and a splash of the cooking water, and serve with the Parmesan grated over.
notes: Times assume the bolognese sauce is already made.

name: Lentil bolognese
summary: Spaghetti with a brown lentil and tomato sauce in place of beef.
method: Reheat the lentil sauce in a small saucepan until bubbling hot, adding a splash of water if it has thickened.
Cook the 180 g dry spaghetti in a large pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, or as the pack says, until al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Toss the spaghetti with the sauce and a splash of the cooking water, and serve with the Parmesan grated over.
notes: A variant of spaghetti bolognese: the lentil tomato sauce replaces the beef bolognese sauce.

name: Mushroom pasta
summary: Egg tagliatelle with browned chestnut mushrooms, garlic, thyme, single cream and Parmesan.
method: Cook the 160 g dry egg tagliatelle in a large pan of boiling water for 6 to 8 minutes, or as the pack says. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.

Meanwhile heat the butter and olive oil in a large frying pan over a high heat and fry the sliced mushrooms for 6 to 8 minutes until browned and their liquid has gone. Add the garlic, thyme, salt and black pepper for 1 minute.
Stir in the single cream and bubble for 1 to 2 minutes, then add the tagliatelle, the grated Parmesan and a splash of the cooking water and toss. Scatter with the chopped parsley.

name: Spinach and ricotta pasta
summary: Farfalle in a no-cook ricotta sauce with wilted spinach, lemon zest and nutmeg.
method: Cook the 180 g dry farfalle in a large pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, or as the pack says, until al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Meanwhile heat the olive oil in a large frying pan, cook the garlic for 1 minute, then add the spinach and stir for 2 minutes until wilted.
Take off the heat and stir in the ricotta, the grated Parmesan, lemon zest, a pinch of nutmeg, the salt and black pepper with 4 to 5 tablespoons of the cooking water to make a creamy sauce.
Toss in the farfalle and serve.

name: Chicken and cream pasta
summary: Penne with golden chicken, onion and garlic in a chicken stock and double cream sauce.
method: Cook the 160 g dry penne in a large pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, or as the pack says, until al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.

Meanwhile cut the chicken breast into bite-sized pieces and season with the salt and black pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan and fry the chicken over a medium-high heat for 5 minutes until golden. Add the chopped onion and garlic and cook for 3 to 4 minutes more until soft and the chicken is cooked through.
Pour in half a stock cube dissolved in 100 ml boiling water and the double cream, and simmer for 3 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir in the grated Parmesan, then the penne and a splash of the cooking water. Scatter with the chopped parsley.

name: Salmon pasta
summary: Linguine with flaked pan-fried salmon, peas, crème fraîche, lemon and dill.
method: Cook the 150 g dry linguine in a large pan of boiling water for 9 to 11 minutes, adding the frozen peas for the last 2 minutes. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.

Meanwhile season the skinless salmon fillets with the salt and black pepper. Heat the olive oil in a frying pan and cook the salmon for 3 to 4 minutes on each side until just cooked, then break into large flakes.
Lower the heat, add the garlic to the pan for 30 seconds, then stir in the crème fraîche, lemon zest, lemon juice and a splash of the cooking water.
Add the linguine and peas, then the salmon and chopped dill, and toss gently.
notes: The crème fraîche record is a proxy (light whipping cream) because USDA has no crème fraîche.

name: Prawn pasta
summary: Spaghetti with garlic and chilli prawns, softened cherry tomatoes, lemon and parsley.
method: Cook the 180 g dry spaghetti in a large pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, or as the pack says, until al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Meanwhile heat the olive oil in a large frying pan, add the sliced garlic and red chilli for 1 minute, then add the halved cherry tomatoes and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until they soften.
Pour in the white wine, if using, and bubble for 1 minute. Add the peeled raw prawns and the salt and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until pink all over.
Toss with the spaghetti, the lemon juice, chopped parsley and a splash of the cooking water.

name: Pasta with peas and ham
summary: Farfalle with peas, cooked ham and spring onions in a light cream and Parmesan sauce.
method: Cook the 180 g dry farfalle in a large pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, adding the frozen peas for the last 3 minutes. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Meanwhile melt the butter in a frying pan and cook the sliced spring onions for 2 minutes, then add the ham, cut into strips, for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the single cream, the grated Parmesan and a splash of the cooking water and bubble for 1 minute. Toss with the farfalle and peas and finish with black pepper.

name: Pasta with roasted vegetables
summary: Penne tossed with oven-roasted courgette, pepper, red onion and cherry tomatoes, finished with feta and basil.
method: Heat the oven to 210°C (190°C fan). Cut the courgette, red pepper and red onion into chunks and toss on a roasting tray with the olive oil, oregano, salt and black pepper. Roast for 20 minutes.
Add the cherry tomatoes and the sliced garlic and roast for 10 minutes more until the vegetables are tender and charred at the edges.
Cook the 180 g dry penne in a large pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, or as the pack says, until al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Toss the penne with the roasted vegetables, their juices and a splash of the cooking water. Crumble the feta over and scatter with torn basil.

name: Spaghetti carbonara
summary: Spaghetti with crisp streaky bacon in a silky sauce of egg, egg yolks, Parmesan and black pepper.
method: Cook the 180 g dry spaghetti in a large pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, or as the pack says, until al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Meanwhile fry the bacon, cut into strips, in a large dry frying pan over a medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes until crisp. Take off the heat.
Beat the egg and egg yolks with the finely grated Parmesan and plenty of black pepper.

Add the spaghetti to the bacon pan (still off the heat) and toss, then pour in the egg mixture with 3 to 4 tablespoons of the cooking water, tossing quickly so the sauce turns creamy without scrambling. Serve at once.
notes: Made with streaky bacon, which is easy to find; pancetta or guanciale work the same way but are not in the catalogue.

name: Pasta with beans
summary: A thick, spoonable stew of macaroni and cannellini beans in a light tomato broth.
method: Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan and cook the finely chopped onion, carrot and celery for 8 to 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the passata, the drained cannellini beans (one 400 g tin) and the vegetable stock and simmer for 10 minutes. Mash about a third of the beans against the side of the pan to thicken the broth.
Add the 150 g dry macaroni and simmer, stirring often, for 10 to 12 minutes until tender, adding a splash of water if it gets too thick. Season with the salt and black pepper.
Serve in bowls with the Parmesan grated over and the chopped parsley.

name: Butternut squash pasta
summary: Fusilli in a smooth sauce of roasted butternut squash, onion, garlic and Parmesan.
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Toss the peeled, cubed butternut squash and the chopped onion with the olive oil, chilli flakes, salt and black pepper on a roasting tray. Roast for 30 to 35 minutes until soft and caramelised at the edges, adding the unpeeled garlic cloves for the last 15 minutes.
Cook the 180 g dry fusilli in a large pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, or as the pack says, until al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Squeeze the garlic from its skins and blend with the squash, onion, grated Parmesan and about 150 ml of the cooking water until smooth.
Toss the sauce with the fusilli, loosening with more cooking water if needed, and scatter with toasted pine nuts if using.
notes: Squash weight is peeled and deseeded (about 600 g as bought).

name: Sausage and broccoli pasta
summary: Penne with browned crumbled pork sausage, broccoli, garlic, chilli and fennel seeds.
method: Cook the 160 g dry penne in a large pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, adding the broccoli florets for the last 4 minutes. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.

Meanwhile heat the olive oil in a large frying pan, squeeze the sausages out of their skins into the pan in small pieces and fry over a medium-high heat for 8 minutes until browned and cooked through. Add the garlic, chilli flakes and fennel seeds for 1 minute.
Add the penne and broccoli with a good splash of the cooking water and toss over the heat for 1 to 2 minutes, breaking up some of the broccoli. Serve with the Parmesan grated over.
notes: The catalogue sausage is a generic pork sausage record; check your sausages' label if they differ.

name: Courgette and lemon pasta
summary: Spaghetti with grated courgettes cooked down in olive oil, lemon, Parmesan and mint.
method: Cook the 180 g dry spaghetti in a large pan of boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, or as the pack says, until al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.

Meanwhile coarsely grate the courgettes. Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat and cook the courgettes with the garlic and salt for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until soft and most of the liquid has gone.
Add the spaghetti, lemon zest, lemon juice, grated Parmesan and a splash of the cooking water and toss until creamy. Finish with black pepper and torn mint.
